  "status": "completed",
  "data": {
    "executiveFinding": "Synthesis: Put the authoritative approval policy and pending-decision state in the sidecar runtime, because it owns the model turn, tool-call identity, run/child-run graph, and durable execution state. Treat the desktop host as a capability-admission and consent enforcement point, not as a second policy engine: it may deny, narrow, or be unavailable, but must never broaden the sidecar decision. Use AG-UI only as the streaming/UI envelope. An approval is a single-use, server-issued capability bound to runId, toolCallId, canonical tool identity and version, exact canonical arguments (or an explicitly re-approved edited-arguments hash), policy version, approver/authentication context, and expiry/nonce. Commit the decision and atomically revalidate those bindings immediately before MCP tools/call; deduplicate execution with an idempotency key. Persist pending decisions and run state, make reconnect independent of the stream, make cancellation explicit, and recover process restarts from durable state. These exact-binding and atomic-commit rules are architecture synthesis derived from the sources; the sources establish the pause/resume, consent, least-privilege, durable-state, and lifecycle primitives but do not prescribe this complete cross-protocol design.",
    "sourceMatrix": [
      {
        "source": "OpenAI Agents SDK — Human-in-the-loop and RunState",
        "url": "https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "Tools can require approval; execution pauses and interruptions expose the agent, tool, and arguments.",
          "The documented flow is to serialize to RunState, approve or reject the pending item, and resume with the original top-level agent.",
          "Approvals are run-wide, including handoffs and nested Agent.as_tool runs; per-call decisions are associated with a call identity, while sticky decisions survive state serialization.",
          "Serialized state contains pending calls, arguments, approvals, and execution data; the SDK warns that snapshots should be trusted or integrity-verified before deserialization.",
          "Runner reconciles the exact pending batch before the next model call without rerunning the tool."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "Model Context Protocol specification — Tools, security, lifecycle, roots, transports",
        "url": "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "MCP says tools are model-controlled, but recommends a human able to deny invocations and clear invocation indicators.",
          "The MCP security guidance says hosts must obtain explicit user consent before invoking tools and before exposing user data; tool annotations are untrusted unless from trusted servers.",
          "Clients and servers must use only successfully negotiated capabilities; roots constrain where servers may operate and should be permissioned, consented, and validated.",
          "MCP transport authorization and host consent are separate concerns; HTTP disconnect should not be interpreted as cancellation, which should be sent explicitly."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "AG-UI Spec 1.0 — Interrupts and lifecycle",
        "url": "https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0/basic/patterns/interrupt-resume",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "A run requiring outside input ends with RUN_FINISHED whose outcome is interrupt, not success.",
          "An interrupted run is closed; continuation is a new run with ResumeEntry values addressing prior interrupt IDs, and every interrupt must be covered.",
          "The producer must not perform an interrupted action because an entry is absent or treat omission as abandonment.",
          "Run lifecycle requires correct start/terminal ordering and forbids ordinary events after closure."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "Microsoft Agent Framework — Human-in-the-loop with AG-UI",
        "url": "https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/integrations/by-component/ui/ag-ui/human-in-the-loop",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "The framework decides whether a tool requires approval; AG-UI transports the request and decision.",
          "The client should reuse the same AgentSession to continue; an approval of false rejects the call, and the approval interrupt includes toolCallId.",
          "Workflow RequestPort pauses execution and pending requests are saved in checkpoints and re-emitted after restoration."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "LangGraph — Interrupts, persistence, re-execution and idempotency",
        "url": "https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/interrupts",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "Interrupts wait for external input and require a checkpointer plus stable thread_id; state is saved and resumed with Command(resume=...).",
          "Production should use a persistent checkpointer; in-memory checkpoints are lost at process restart.",
          "After an interrupt or retry, the containing node runs again from the start; side effects must therefore be idempotent, using mechanisms such as idempotency keys, upserts, or read-before-write checks.",
          "Replay re-executes post-checkpoint work and interrupts and is not an exactly-once side-effect guarantee."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "Temporal — Workflows and approval pattern",
        "url": "https://docs.temporal.io/design-patterns/approval",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "The approval pattern blocks workflow execution until an external Signal carrying decision, approver details, and comments arrives, with timeout/escalation behavior.",
          "Temporal rebuilds workflow state from ordered event history after crashes; outside-world operations belong in Activities and workflow code must be deterministic.",
          "Activities may re-execute and should be idempotent; cancellation is explicit and Activity heartbeat/handling is needed to stop work.",
          "Continue-As-New preserves state while starting a fresh execution and pending Signals must be drained before completion or Continue-As-New."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "OWASP LLM01:2025 and LLM06:2025",
        "url": "https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "OWASP recommends least privilege, per-user context/minimum scopes, human approval for high-impact actions, and authorization in downstream systems rather than relying on the LLM.",
          "OWASP recommends complete mediation so every extension request is checked against security policy and highlights prompt injection, compromised extensions, and excessive agency."
        ]
      },
      {
        "source": "A2A Protocol Specification",
        "url": "https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/",
        "normativeFindings": [
          "A2A separates stateful Task lifecycle from streams: input-required and auth-required are interrupted states; completed, failed, canceled, and rejected are terminal.",
          "A task can continue using the same taskId/contextId; SubscribeToTask returns current state first, and cancellation is an idempotent best-effort attempt.",
          "Streams may be disconnected or concurrent without changing task state; resubscription does not establish a universal missed-event replay guarantee.",
          "A2A supports authorization chains between agents, but does not define a general parent-child run graph or automatic propagation semantics."
        ]
      }
    ],
    "invariants": [
      "Only the sidecar policy engine may create, resolve, expire, or mutate a pending approval; the host may enforce admission and deny, but cannot approve an unapproved call or broaden a policy decision.",
      "No tool side effect occurs before approval (when required), host capability admission, downstream authorization, and final atomic revalidation all succeed.",
      "Every decision binds to immutable runId, parent/child run identity, toolCallId, canonical tool/server identity, tool version or schema digest, exact canonical arguments hash, policy version, authenticated approver, decision time, nonce, and expiry. Edited arguments create a new proposal/hash and require explicit approval.",
      "The host must check the exact sidecar-issued capability immediately before forwarding MCP tools/call; a UI preview, tool discovery result, or earlier check is never sufficient. Changes to tool schema, server identity, roots, user/session authorization, or policy invalidate the decision.",
      "Approvals are single-use and atomically consumed with creation of an idempotency-keyed execution record; duplicates return the recorded outcome and never invoke the external tool twice.",
      "Pending decisions and run state are durable, integrity-protected, access-controlled, and recoverable independently of AG-UI connection state; untrusted serialized state is rejected.",
      "Disconnect is not approval and is not cancellation. Cancellation is an explicit state transition that prevents future execution and propagates to children where supported; in-flight external effects may require compensation and must report best-effort cancellation.",
      "A child run/tool call has its own identity and approval binding while inheriting parent authorization constraints; parent cancellation, policy revocation, and terminal state prevent child execution.",
      "Every state transition is auditable with proposal, exact arguments, policy version, decision/approver, host admission, execution attempt, result, and reason; secrets are minimized/redacted."
    ],
    "recommendedArchitecture": [
      "Sidecar: own model calls, canonical tool-call construction, policy evaluation, pending-decision store, run/child-run state machine, durable checkpoints, approval capability issuance, audit log, and final authorization gate.",
      "Desktop host: own local MCP process lifecycle, negotiated capability/resource/root admission, OS/user authentication, UI consent rendering, sandboxing, and a fail-closed forwarding proxy. It can apply a stricter local deny rule, but must not turn a sidecar deny/pending result into approval or silently rewrite arguments.",
      "AG-UI: carry RUN_STARTED/TOOL_CALL events and an interrupt-shaped approval request; terminate the interrupted run correctly and resume with a new run referencing the interrupt. Use an application-level cursor/state fetch for reconnect rather than assuming SSE replay.",
      "Use an approval object such as {decisionId, runId, childRunId, toolCallId, toolRef, toolVersion/schemaHash, argsHash, policyVersion, approver, issuedAt, expiresAt, nonce, signature}; keep canonical original arguments and any edited replacement separately.",
      "Admission flow: sidecar discovers/validates tool and policy, freezes canonical proposal, persists PENDING, emits AG-UI interrupt; host authenticates reviewer and checks negotiated capability/server/root/user scope; decision returns to sidecar; sidecar atomically validates binding and consumes capability; host rechecks and forwards exactly that call; sidecar records result.",
      "Use durable checkpoint/event history (Temporal-style or persistent LangGraph/OpenAI RunState storage), optimistic version/compare-and-swap on pending decisions, and idempotency keys at both host proxy and downstream tool where possible.",
      "For restart, reload nonterminal state and re-emit pending decisions with the same decision identity but a new stream/run envelope; never auto-approve. For detach/reconnect, query current run and pending decision, reconcile by IDs/version, then subscribe again.",
      "For child runs, maintain explicit parentRunId and childRunId, aggregate policy constraints downward, and require each child call to be authorized in its own context. Treat A2A contextId/referenceTaskIds as correlation, not proof of approval inheritance."
    ],
    "stateMachine": [
      "PROPOSED: sidecar receives a model tool call; canonicalize tool identity, schema/version, and arguments; assign runId/childRunId/toolCallId and compute argsHash.",
      "ADMITTED_BY_POLICY or DENIED_BY_POLICY: evaluate sidecar policy, user/downstream scope, risk, and current tool metadata. A deny is terminal for that proposal; never ask the host to override it.",
      "PENDING_APPROVAL: persist the complete immutable proposal and policyVersion transactionally; emit AG-UI interrupt with decisionId/toolCallId and human-readable details. Do not invoke MCP.",
      "HOST_CHECKED: host authenticates the user, confirms the currently negotiated MCP capability/server/root/session scope, and records a local admission. Host denial, disconnect, expiry, or policy change leaves the call blocked.",
      "DECISION_RECEIVED: sidecar accepts only an authenticated, unexpired, nonce-bearing decision that addresses the exact pending decision and policy version; missing/duplicate/mismatched submissions are rejected idempotently.",
      "REVALIDATING: atomically compare-and-swap PENDING to EXECUTING while rechecking policy, capability epoch, tool/schema digest, argsHash, user/session, parent state, cancellation, and expiry. If any changes, return STALE/REAPPROVAL_REQUIRED.",
      "EXECUTING: host forwards the exact canonical call once with idempotency key; sidecar treats MCP result as an external effect and records it. A transport disconnect does not imply cancellation.",
      "SUCCEEDED or FAILED: persist result/error and publish tool result/AG-UI continuation. Duplicate approval or retry reads the recorded execution outcome.",
      "CANCELED/EXPIRED/REJECTED/STALE: persist terminal reason, prevent invocation, notify UI, and require a newly proposed call for changed arguments/policy/tool metadata.",
      "DETACHED/RECONNECTING and PROCESS_RESTART: keep the durable state unchanged, recover by run/decision IDs, re-emit current pending state, and resume only after an explicit valid decision; terminal runs cannot be restarted."
    ],
    "rejectedAlternatives": [
      "Host-only approval policy: rejected because the host does not own model/run/child-run state and can approve a stale or mismatched proposal; use host admission as defense in depth, not the authority.",
      "Sidecar-only approval with unrestricted host forwarding: rejected because MCP explicitly treats host consent, capability negotiation, roots, and local tool execution as host responsibilities; the host must still fail closed.",
      "Approval as a boolean for tool name or UI label: rejected because it is vulnerable to argument substitution, tool/version changes, confused deputy behavior, TOCTOU, and replay.",
      "Re-running the model after approval or reconstructing the call from UI fields: rejected because it can change toolCallId/arguments and produce a different action; resume the persisted pending state.",
      "Treating AG-UI/SSE disconnect as cancellation or relying on stream replay: rejected because AG-UI closes interrupted runs, MCP distinguishes disconnect from cancellation, and A2A does not guarantee missed-event replay.",
      "In-memory pending approvals or desktop-only state: rejected because process restart loses decisions/checkpoints; use durable, integrity-protected sidecar state.",
      "Assuming approval makes external execution exactly once: rejected because LangGraph and Temporal document re-execution/retries; require idempotency keys/deduplication and explicit compensation.",
      "Treating MCP tool metadata, model instructions, or A2A contextId as authorization: rejected because MCP annotations can be untrusted, OWASP requires downstream complete mediation, and context/correlation IDs do not establish approval inheritance."
    ],
    "openQuestions": [
      "What exact canonicalization and schema-digest algorithm will both sidecar and host implement, including JSON number/string normalization and secret redaction without changing the authorized bytes?",
      "Which actions require approval, which may use bounded sticky approval, and what is the maximum TTL/epoch for a capability after tool metadata, roots, credentials, or policy change?",
      "How will reviewer authentication, authorization, multi-party/quorum approval, delegated approval, and audit retention be implemented on the desktop host and sidecar?",
      "What MCP servers/tools are idempotent, and what compensating transaction exists for non-idempotent effects when cancellation or process failure occurs after forwarding?",
      "What durable store/event log, locking/CAS mechanism, encryption, key rotation, and crash-consistency protocol will protect pending decisions and prevent two host processes from executing one approval?",
      "How are parent cancellation, policy revocation, child-run failure, timeout, and partially completed parallel tool calls aggregated and surfaced to the user?",
      "Will the deployment implement an explicit AG-UI reconnect cursor/state endpoint, or use A2A-style task retrieval/resubscription plus authoritative sidecar state to reconcile missed events?",
      "How are local MCP server upgrades, tool-list changes, root changes, and capability renegotiation propagated to invalidate pending approvals?"
    ]
  },
  "model": "spark-2",
  "threadId": "01a0d547-91eb-778a-a4cf-7bb61f24ddec",
  "threadTurn": 1,
  "mode": "extract",
  "message": "Compiled an authoritative-source comparison and clearly marked architecture synthesis versus normative source findings. The exact-binding/TOCTOU protocol is a recommended synthesis because no single cited standard specifies the complete cross-protocol design.",
  "suggestions": [
    {
      "label": "Approval threat model",
      "prompt": "Can you turn the invariants into a concrete threat model and abuse-case test plan?"
    },
    {
      "label": "Protocol schema",
      "prompt": "Can you draft JSON schemas for the approval proposal, decision capability, and execution record?"
    },
    {
      "label": "Failure testing",
      "prompt": "Can you produce a failure-injection matrix covering reconnects, crashes, retries, cancellation, and tool changes?"
    }
  ],
  "expiresAt": "2026-09-25T21:17:12.497Z",
  "creditsUsed": 0
}
